**Description**

The Data Analyst II oversees activities related to data integrity, security and enhancement of the value of data. The Data Analyst II may direct the movement of data across multiple systems; oversee its validation and organization and make sure that data is available to appropriate people and systems within an organization. The Data Analyst II will also develop and execute reports that will be important assets of the practice as they continue to develop and evaluate a new model of care.

The Department of Population Health Science and Policy is seeking a Data Analyst II to work on projects related to maternal health policy and equity, pregnancy-related influences to lifecourse cardiometabolic disease, school-level influences on adolescent preconception health, economic evaluation, and health services research. The Data Analyst II will be an integral member of our research teams, and will collaborate with study investigators (including epidemiologists, health economists, OBGYNs, etc), and other research team members on projects related to maternal health disparities and inequities. This is a one-year position with an opportunity for longer-term renewal.

The ideal candidate would be: 1) highly motivated and responsible; 2) an effective communicator; 3) extremely organized and detail-oriented; 4) someone who combines initiative with responsiveness to supervision; 5) someone comfortable asking questions and eager to learn; and, 6) flexible and able to shift gears as new tasks present themselves. Opportunities exist for mentorship and professional development for Data Analysts.

  
**Responsibilities**

* Plan, organize, conduct, and communicate data-intensive analysis and research within the overall scope of cardiovascular disease prevention, economic evaluation, maternal health disparities, and health equity.
* Develop required research skills in health services research and quantitative analysis
* Engage in data management, regression-based data analysis, and manuscript writing
* Guide and mentor research interns
* Communicate and work with internal and external collaborators.

  
**Qualifications**

* Bachelors degree in computer science, statistics and/or related field required, or combination of equivalent work experience and education. Masters degree in relevant field of study preferred (e.g., statistics, epidemiology, computer science, etc.).
* 3+ years of analytics experience including report development and database application/management experience, preferably in a large medical center or healthcare environment

**Preferred:**

* Strong quantitative skills and proficiency working with data analysis tools such as STATA, SAS, and R.
    
* Excellent written and oral communication skills.
    
* Highly motivated and interested in developing a research career.
    
* Able to work independently in a multidisciplinary setting.
    
* Experience working with systems science modelling methodologies such as system dynamics and agent-based modelling is not required but a plus.

Job Description

Asset Management - Data Analyst, Private Markets Data Products (Vice President)

Job summary

As a Data Analyst on the Asset Management Private Markets Data Products team, you will serve as the Alternatives data subject-matter expert for the domain. You will help build out the Private Markets data model and the semantic layer that sits on top of it, standardizing definitions and making data consistently usable by both people and AI. Your primary focus will be expanding Alternatives datasets to include the business-critical attributes that support core business processes and downstream consumption. You will enable client and investor reporting, oversee business-as-usual data issues and data quality, help scale the platform, and ensure data is delivered accurately to the appropriate Systems of Record (SORs). This is a hands-on, analytical role that depends on sustained collaboration with internal and external partners to understand the underlying businesses, the data they produce, and how consumers need to use it.

Job responsibilities

Serve as the Alternatives data subject-matter expert for the Private Markets domain, acting as the reference point for what a data element means, where it originates, how it behaves, and how it should be used.

Build out the Private Markets data model alongside engineering and architecture partners, defining entities, attributes, relationships, grain, and lineage, including net-new datasets where no prior model exists.

Develop and maintain the semantic layer over the data model, covering standardized business definitions, derived metrics, and consistent vocabularies, so that data is directly consumable by people, BI tools, and AI agents without re-interpretation.

Expand Alternatives datasets to capture business-critical attributes, sequencing coverage by the core business processes and downstream consumption each attribute unlocks.

Partner with engineering in an agile framework to plan and deliver strategic work: shaping epics and stories in JIRA, authoring and reviewing data requirements and mapping specifications, answering domain questions through development, and participating in UAT and control testing.

Systematically connect vendors, fund administrators, custodians, general partners, and other external sources into the platform, onboarding feeds in a repeatable way that continues to build out the Alternatives data core rather than accumulating one-off extracts, and working with those partners to interpret data, validate it, and resolve discrepancies at source.

Partner closely with the Chief Data Office to ensure the domain adheres to firmwide and Asset Management data governance and data strategy principles, covering data ownership, classification, quality standards, documentation expectations, and the domain's contribution to enterprise data priorities.

Enable client, investor, and management reporting by translating reporting requirements into data requirements, sourcing the underlying attributes, and validating outputs against expected results.

Own business-as-usual data issue management and data quality: triage and root-cause issues, define and monitor business data quality rules and thresholds, drive remediation with source and platform teams, and surface recurring themes for structural fixes.

Ensure data is delivered accurately and completely to the appropriate Systems of Record, and support migration from legacy sources to strategic SORs including mapping, reconciliation, and cutover validation.

Profile and analyze data hands-on to test hypotheses, size gaps, and quantify impact, providing the evidence that informs prioritization, roadmap, and design decisions.

Maintain domain documentation covering data dictionaries, business glossary entries, data quality rules, lineage, and catalog and metadata entries, so the domain stays self-describing as it grows.

Help scale the platform by identifying reusable patterns and standards rather than one-off fixes as additional businesses, asset classes, and datasets onboard.

Required qualifications, skills and capabilities

Extensive experience in data-focused roles such as data analysis, data management, data operations, or business and data product analysis, within financial services or a comparably complex data environment.

Deep, practical knowledge of private markets or alternatives data and the businesses that produce it. We will also consider an exceptional data analyst from an adjacent domain who can demonstrate they learn a new business quickly and thoroughly.

Experience acting as the primary data expert for a business area or dataset, including owning its definitions and documentation and fielding questions from partner teams.

Strong hands-on analytical skills, comfortable working directly with data to profile, reconcile, and investigate, using SQL or equivalent query and analysis tooling.

Experience translating business needs into data requirements: attributes, definitions, models, and mapping specifications that engineers can build from without ambiguity.

Rigor and ownership around data quality, with a track record of driving issues to root cause and to closure across teams rather than handing them off.

Strong written communication, able to document definitions and decisions clearly enough that others can rely on them without a conversation.

Collaborative operator who works effectively across business, operations, technology, and external partners, and can move between detailed data work and senior stakeholder discussion.

Comfort with ambiguity and greenfield work, able to bring structure where no model, dictionary, or precedent yet exists.

Preferred qualifications, skills and capabilities

Subject matter expertise in private markets data domains including capital calls and distributions, waterfalls and carried interest, NAV and performance, commitments and unfunded capital, investor, fund and entity structures, and deal and portfolio company data.

Experience supporting Real Estate, Infrastructure, Private Credit, Private Equity, or Alternative Solutions businesses.

Technical depth is a strong plus: advanced SQL, Python, cloud data platforms such as AWS and Snowflake, transformation tooling, and data catalog or lineage solutions.

Aptitude for AI tooling, particularly applied to data modeling and to building reusable skills and agents, with a readiness to adopt new and innovative tools to execute on deliverables and strategic projects.

Experience building or contributing to a semantic layer, metrics store, or business glossary that serves BI, self-service analytics, or AI consumption.

Experience with fund administrator, general partner, custodian, or vendor data feeds and the reconciliation and validation that comes with them.

Experience supporting client or investor reporting within an asset manager.

Familiarity with data governance concepts including data ownership, reference data and MDM, metadata, data contracts, and controls.

High aptitude with agile collaboration tools such as Confluence and JIRA, and experience working alongside a product owner and an engineering squad.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience; diverse academic backgrounds welcome. CFA, CAIA, or similar credential is a plus.

Duties Description
Strategic Planning and Innovation performs management activities designed to set priorities, focus energy and resources, strengthen operations, and ensure that employees and other stakeholders are working together to achieve measurable results. This office is providing project oversight for several initiatives that will transform the way the Department delivers services to partner agencies and to the public, and this position will play an important role in ensuring the success of these modernization efforts.

The Data Analyst 4 duties in the office of Strategic Planning and Innovation will include but are not limited to the following:

• Oversee staff in development and execution of data analytics solutions for the agency, including the development of data dashboards for executives.
• Direct staff in the evaluation of current approaches and establishment of standards and metrics.
• Oversee staff in the identification and testing of system changes that will impact data analysis capabilities.
• Manage staff in the development of reports for department executives and the Governor’s staff.
• Collaborate with program administrators in the completion of agency wide reports.
• Manage staff in the preparation of data for internal and external requests.
• Oversee staff in the development of the DCS strategic plan and monitoring associated metrics.
• Provide advice and consultation to agency management on program operations.
• Manage staff in the identification of new training needed by the agency.
• Manage staff in training development and delivery.
• Supervise a team of data analysts.

Non-competitive: eleven years of experience* in data visualization, and statistical models and data mining tools. Two years of the experience must have been at a managerial level.
